metadata.note: A CLI-explainer weekly recap -- a NEW week's log, separate from the earlier recaps (weekly-recap-brand-check and before). Same story spine as those builds (B00 cold open -> problem -> ask -> code -> output -> change -> code -> output -> lesson -> handoff -> outro; real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat; one required revision cycle). weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run; v1 is a flat list of four parts, v2 adds a STATUS to each (published / produced / ongoing / saved) and prints a done-vs-ongoing count ('3 parts done, 1 ongoing') -- chosen because the user asked for an honest update and the Homes of Hope outreach is ongoing, not finished. THE OUTREACH IS NOT DESCRIBED beyond 'posting and outreach with Yatra, ongoing' (user instruction), and it carries the user's required label, 'Homes of Hope documentary outreach (with Yatra)'. HOMES OF HOPE VISUALS ARE ABSTRACT (user instruction): connected dots around a megaphone, no photos, no children, no people shapes. NO real platform logos: the Substack article is a mock header (text kicker only), GitHub is a generic code-folder icon with a plain-text label. Video count: the user says 'two videos on Brutalist ... each exported in both 16:9 and 9:16, for four files in total'; this recap uses that wording exactly (two videos: this week's AI topic video and this recap; four files). Disclosed substitutions carried forward: (1) af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default voice/handle; (2) rendered through run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py. Self-intro ('Hi, I'm Agrima') opens B00's narration per the user's kickoff. All items are the user's own self-reported account. The 'all project files pushed to GitHub' claim is the user's statement; this toolkit session had not pushed this week's foundation-search files when the video was built. No footage exists -- every visual is a generated Manim graphic.

WEEK = [
    {"part": "1. Writing",
     "item": "Published my weekly article on Substack: 'Your Foundation Search Is Doing Market Research'"},
    {"part": "2. Video production",
     "item": "Two Brutalist videos (AI topic + weekly recap), each in 16:9 and 9:16: four files"},
    {"part": "3. Homes of Hope documentary",
     "item": "Continued the posting and outreach with Yatra"},
    {"part": "4. Organizing the work",
     "item": "Pushed all of my project files to GitHub"},
]


def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"- {entry['part']}: {entry['item']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    log()

props.title: weekly_recap_v2.py
props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"status": "published", "part": "1. Writing",
     "item": "Weekly article on Substack: 'Your Foundation Search Is Doing Market Research'"},
    {"status": "produced", "part": "2. Video production",
     "item": "Two Brutalist videos, each in 16:9 and 9:16: four files"},
    {"status": "ongoing", "part": "3. Homes of Hope documentary",
     "item": "Posting and outreach, with Yatra"},
    {"status": "saved", "part": "4. Organizing the work",
     "item": "All project files on GitHub"},
]


def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"[{entry['status'].upper()}] {entry['part']}: {entry['item']}")
    ongoing = [e for e in WEEK if e["status"] == "ongoing"]
    print(f"{len(WEEK) - len(ongoing)} parts done, {len(ongoing)} ongoing")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    log()
